title: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
why_read: A genuinely concerning security finding showing that backdoors can transfer efficiently from teacher to student models during a popular LLM training technique, relevant to anyone deploying distilled models.
analysis: On-policy distillation trains a smaller student model using live feedback generated by a larger teacher model, and this paper shows that if the teacher has a hidden backdoor, that backdoor can transfer to the student even with very few poisoned examples. The researchers trace the mechanism to subtle differences in the teacher's output probabilities between normal and trigger-containing inputs, which get absorbed into the student's internal representations during training. They also propose a mitigation that suppresses this anomalous signal at the source. This is a meaningful supply-chain security result for the AI training pipeline, since it implies that using an untrusted teacher model for distillation carries real backdoor risk.
